# LinStabPy

> Sparse linear stability and resolvent analysis of compressible viscous flows. Python toolkit (CLI + library) that builds the linearized compressible Navier-Stokes operator on 2D structured base flows and solves eigenvalue and resolvent problems through PETSc/SLEPc with MUMPS sparse-direct factorization.

LinStabPy answers two questions about a steady flow field you supply: stability (does a small disturbance grow on its own, at what frequency, with what shape?) and resolvent (at a given frequency, which harmonic forcing produces the largest response?). Base flows are loaded from files, never computed here. Cases are defined in YAML; results land in contract-stable `.npz` archives.

How to use this file: find the task below, follow the link, and read that page. Links point at human-readable HTML pages; each page's Markdown source lives in the repo under `docs/pages/`.

Critical facts agents get wrong: the `linstabpy` CLI takes NO case arguments -- config and output travel by `LINSTABPY_CASE_CONFIG` and `LINSTABPY_CASE_OUTPUT_NPZ` env vars, and unknown CLI bare words and `--flags` warn on stderr but are otherwise ignored (`parse_known_args`, exit code unchanged), so a guessed command still runs the wrong case. Install is the hard part (one MPI stack, complex-scalar PETSc/SLEPc + MUMPS via `install.sh --diagnose` -> `install.sh` -> `install.sh --check`); nothing that solves will work until `--check` passes. On macOS always use `.venv/bin/python`, never `uv run`. Fixed conventions repo-wide: temporal eigenvalues `omega = eig(i*L0)` with `exp(-i*omega*t)` time dependence, unstable exactly when `Im(omega) > 0`; SBP orders are 2, 4, 6, 8 only; default shifted solve is `KSPPREONLY` + `PCLU` through MUMPS.

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/getting-started/): Install, first runs (example 0 needs no data), the example family, your first own case. Read this before running anything.
- [Boundary interfaces](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/boundaries/): The machine surface: env-var CLI, YAML case schema, Python lazy imports, file inputs, NPZ outputs. Required reading for agents driving runs.
- [Core concepts](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/core-concepts/): Exact definitions of base flow, growth rate, gain, Chu norm, wavemaker, sponge. Open beside any science page.
- [FAQ](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/faq/): Which analysis do I need, shift-branch confusion, dissipation on/off, sawtooth wiggles, cache-valid surprise.

## Reference

- [Architecture](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/architecture/): Packages, who owns which policy, run order (config to baseflow to mesh to L0 + BCs to factorize to eigen/resolvent to payload), stored data, quality gates.
- [Modules](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/modules/): One page per package (driver, operators, BC recipes, mesh, baseflow, config, stability, resolvent, solvers and router, linalg, utilities): a short summary, then the package notes.
- [Solver glossary](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/solver-glossary/): Every KSP, PC, EPS, ST, and MatShell term defined from zero with official PETSc/SLEPc links.

## Optional

- [References](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/references/): Papers and manuals behind the wiki, grouped by what they justify.
- [Installation](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/installation/): Full install guide: install.sh, conda, macOS, clusters, Intel MPI, GPU stacks, MPI rules.
- [Troubleshooting](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/troubleshooting/): Known install and runtime failures with their fixes, and what to send when a machine is still broken.
- [Development workflow](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/development/development/): Branches, tests, changelog, release steps, and how the generated wiki files are checked.
- [Compute backends](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/development/compute-backends/): Factor backend audit: MUMPS default, cuDSS, STRUMPACK, SuperLU_DIST, version floors, measured evidence.
- [Runtime NPZ contract](https://linstabpy.vercel.app/development/runtime-npz-contract/): Key groups of the result archive and the rules for changing them.
- [Repository README](https://github.com/openfluids/linstabpy#readme): Short install, example runner, numerical setup, parity with LinStab2D.
